recommendation: Keep this audit as-is and do not re-remove protocol from current core source for FHIR-15163. Future PlanDefinitionType code changes should go through THO/UTG and account for both the original FHIR-15163 narrowing and the later FHIR-23876 broadening.
issue_request: FHIR-15163 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request for PlanDefinition asking to remove the generic plan-definition-type code protocol, add clinical-protocol and workflow-definition with specified definitions, and update PlanDefinition.type to describe a high-level category distinguishing interested systems.
initial_application: The issue was applied historically in SVN 13290, represented by git commit a1cc4ed53f2d5cbc4633b5869d6c58d983fc81ef, which named GF#15163, changed a PlanDefinition example from protocol to clinical-protocol, and updated the old spreadsheet source. Later source refactors preserved the requested PlanDefinition.type definition, and terminology moved from local core value set XML to THO.
additional_context: FHIR-23876 later approved broadening clinical-protocol back to protocol for lab, technical, study, and other non-clinical protocol use cases. UP-655 implemented the protocol code in THO, and the combined branch already contains the FHIR-23876 reconciliation commit 48800791108c29d64806ea95c093c6c5c0f41f74 fixing the active PlanDefinition protocol example. Current THO PlanDefinitionType includes protocol, clinical-protocol, and workflow-definition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active core source has PlanDefinition in build scope, PlanDefinition.type has the requested high-level definition and binds to the THO plan-definition-type value set, and there is no active local core PlanDefinition type value set source to edit.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied/Persuasive CDS issue broadened PlanDefinition type semantics by adding protocol back after FHIR-15163 had introduced clinical-protocol.
UTG proposal implemented the FHIR-23876 protocol code addition in THO for PlanDefinitionType.
